title: Sell Mineral Rights in Shepherd, MT
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Shepherd, MT
metaDescription: Shepherd, MT sits east of Billings on Yellowstone County farm and ranch ground. I buy mineral interests here based on real title and lease history, not guesswork.
heroLead: Shepherd sits close enough to Billings that people assume the oil activity from elsewhere in the state reaches out here. It generally doesn't.
intro: Shepherd is farm and ranch country east of Billings, and when I run title on parcels out here, what I usually find is a quiet mineral estate — no active lease, no recent drilling, a homestead-era severance sitting undisturbed for a generation or two. That's a common and entirely normal situation for this part of Yellowstone County. It just means I evaluate the interest for what it is rather than pricing it like ground in an active play.
I still take these calls seriously. Quiet ground has a real, defensible value, even if it's a different number than what a family sometimes hopes to hear at the start of the conversation.

sections.heading: What I check first
paragraphs: Before I discuss a number, I confirm the legal description against the county record, check whether there's a lease on file, active or expired, and look at whether any operator has shown recent interest in the area. Shepherd-area interests are usually valued on that documented history, not on speculation.

sections.heading: Family land that's been split by inheritance
paragraphs: A fair number of the calls I get from around Shepherd come from heirs who inherited a fractional share of a parcel their grandparents or great-grandparents homesteaded, often alongside several cousins they've never met. I handle that kind of multi-heir situation regularly and can usually confirm your specific share faster than the family expects.

faqs.question: Is there active drilling near Shepherd?
faqs.answer: Generally no. This is farm and ranch country with limited historical mineral development. I confirm the status on your specific parcel before quoting.

faqs.question: My interest is split among several cousins — can you still buy my share?
faqs.answer: Yes. I buy individual fractional shares directly and don't require the whole family to sell together.

faqs.question: How do you determine what a quiet, unleased interest is worth?
faqs.answer: I look at the recorded lease history, any nearby activity, and general area trends, then price it as long-term potential rather than current income.

faqs.question: Do you buy interests even if my family has never dealt with them before?
faqs.answer: Yes, that's common with older Shepherd-area homestead interests. I do the initial title work so you're not starting from scratch.

faqs.question: How quickly can a sale on a quiet Shepherd-area interest actually close?
faqs.answer: Once title is confirmed clean, it moves fast. Most of the time is spent up front verifying the chain, not negotiating a number.
